Auto-summary (auto-generated): TerraBridge wants fast pilot; legal asks for DPA clarity; SE flagged KV-cache and quantization for latency targets; FinOps wants committed pricing to compare to BigCloudAI quote.

00:00 Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Jordan Hayes from Redwood, AE. Mira my solutions engineer is here, and Diego from success. How's everybody?
00:14 Samir: Hey, Samir Khatri, hi. We're good, thanks. Looking to make this as quick as possible, we've got exec ask to move in three weeks.
00:22 Lina: Lina here, legal. We'll be focusing on the DPA and a couple of MSA clauses — audit logs, data residency, egress; want to flag up front.
00:30 Daniel: Daniel Park, CTO. Technical folks are mostly curious about latency SLOs and what dedicated looks like.
00:36 Olivia: Olivia Chen, FinOps. We'll need committed pricing and a clear billing cadence.
00:42 Jordan: Great. Quick agenda: 1) legal lanes — MSA/DPA, 2) SLA and pricing, 3) technical handoff and benchmark plan. Mira will cover technicals.

02:05 Mira: Quick note — from the SE side, Dedicated means reserved GPU pools, predictable throughput. We can guarantee throughput targets in the SLA for dedicated configs; for hosted we have better time-to-value but less strict SLAs. For your latency target, what are you shooting for?
02:21 Daniel: We're looking for 95th perc under 120ms p50-ish ideally for short prompts.
02:30 Mira: Okay, that's realistic on a 2x A100 or H100ish pool with the right batching and KV caching. There's some work to do on quantization; we can demo performance numbers in a preflight.

05:00 Samir: From procurement — timeline is tight. We need to know which clauses will likely be redlined. Lina, do you want to go through the MSA hot spots?
05:12 Lina: Sure. Main items: indemnity cap, data processing scope, KMS control, egress fees, audit rights, and termination for convenience timelines. Two big DPA asks: 1) customer-managed keys or equivalent (we know Redwood offers KMS integration) and 2) stricter data retention and deletion language.
05:35 Jordan: We support KMS integrations; we have docs on customer-managed keys. On retention, we can commit to configurable retention windows and delete on request, but we'll need the standard DPA language redline.
05:47 Lina: Also want a clear statement about audit logs and retention for a minimum of 2 years for transaction traces.
06:00 Diego: Note that we can surface logs through the Console with token-level tracing; Mira can show that in the preflight.

08:10 Olivia: Pricing — we got an initial quote from BigCloudAI at a committed rate; how does Redwood price dedicated? Is there a ramp or minimum term?
08:25 Jordan: Dedicated is typically reserved monthly or annually; we can do a short pilot commit (30 days) with a pro-rated fee, or a month-to-month with a higher unit price. For pilot we usually propose a 30-day reserved pool to get SLAs. We'll send a committed-rate spreadsheet.

10:15 Lina: On liability, we have a couple of non-negotiables around data residency and export controls — TerraBridge handles regulated financial data, so egress and cross-border must be explicit.
10:30 Jordan: Understood. We have region controls and private deployment options; for pilot we can limit to a single EU region or single US region depending on your needs.

12:00 Mira: Technical note — if you need private deployment we can do Private (VPC or on-prem) which brings a slightly different onboarding and licensing model; Dedicated is still hosted but isolated. For throughput and 120ms 95th, Dedicated in-region should work.
12:28 Daniel: If we go Private there's an extra compliance window — does that push the timeline?
12:34 Mira: Potentially, yes. Private on-prem requires packaging and network review; VPC-hosted Private has a faster path. For a three-week pilot, VPC or Dedicated hosted is more realistic.

15:00 Samir: Ok so immediate blockers: Lina's redlines, pricing confirmation, and a technical preflight. If we get those in place this week we can present to execs.

16:10 Jordan: We'll do that. I'll get redlined MSA + a DPA matrix to you. We should call out KMS, egress, and audit logs in that doc.

18:20 Lina: Quick question — can Redwood accept some DPA appendices, rather than changing baseline terms? That's sometimes easier for us.
18:30 Jordan: Yes, appendices are fine; we'll propose a DPA appendix for TerraBridge-specific controls.

20:15 Mira: For benchmarks, we suggest these steps: 1) you provide a small representative dataset and token distribution, 2) Redwood runs a Dedicated preflight with KV-cache enabled, 3) we produce a runbook with observed p50/p95 and cost per 1k tokens. We'll need about 2-3 hours of data prep from your side.
20:40 Daniel: We can do a subset of prod traffic, scrubbed. We'll aim to deliver that by Thursday.

23:00 Olivia: Billing cadence — we need clear terms for egress, storage, and committed capacity. Any hidden surcharges?
23:12 Jordan: We'll itemize egress by region, storage by retention window, and committed capacity as a monthly reserved fee. No surprise surcharges but there are standard overage rates. We'll put those in the pricing spreadsheet.

25:40 Samir: On approvals — procurement needs legal signoff and FinOps signoff. What's typical approval lead time?
25:52 Lina: For DPA redlines we usually need 3-5 business days to review, faster if the vendor responds quickly.
26:05 Olivia: FinOps will need the committed-rate comparison to BigCloudAI; we can turn around approval in 48-72 hours if pricing is competitive.

28:10 Mira: Technical question from my side — what models are you evaluating and expected RPS? This affects batching and instance sizing.
28:22 Daniel: Primarily a Llama-variant internally tuned, about 20 RPC/s at peak for the pilot, average prompt length short, 100-120 tokens.
28:35 Mira: Got it, that aligns with a small Dedicated pool. We'll size an initial 4-GPU pool and report.

31:00 Lina: A specific clause: can Redwood commit to notifying TerraBridge within 24 hours of a security incident that materially affects data?
31:12 Jordan: Yes we have an incident notification process; 24-hour notification is standard in our enterprise playbook. We'll include that in the DPA appendix.

33:50 Daniel: Any fallbacks if Dedicated capacity is constrained during pilot? We need resilience plan.
33:58 Mira: We can define a fallback policy: route to a compatible hosted instance with throttling and notify via webhook. For pilot we'll allocate dedicated so constraint risk is low.

36:40 Samir: Procurement question — is there a PO requirement to start the pilot?
36:46 Jordan: For a reserved Dedicated pilot we typically require a PO or a signed SOW covering the reserved capacity. If you prefer, we can start with a credit-based hosted trial with less strict SLA.

38:30 Lina: Regarding audit logs retention, can Redwood provide immutable logs for 2 years? Or at least cryptographically verifiable traces?
38:46 Diego: We can export logs to customer S3 with object versioning; cryptographic verifiability is on the roadmap — we can support signed export timestamps today.

40:10 Jordan: Recap: Redwood will send redlined MSA + DPA appendix, SE will run preflight benchmark after TerraBridge shares scrubbed dataset, Pricing to send committed-rate spreadsheet comparing hosted vs dedicated and a 30-day pilot option. We'll also include a fallback routing policy.

42:00 Olivia: Great. If pricing is in line with BigCloudAI we'll move quickly.

43:20 Lina: I'll send non-negotiable DPA points by Friday. I may also ask for a short legal-team-to-legal-team call if we hit redlines.

44:10 Jordan: Sounds good. Mira, any final technical notes?
44:15 Mira: I'll put together a runbook and checklist for network whitelisting, KMS set up, and dataset ingestion. Expect an invite for the benchmark run.

47:30 Daniel: One more — any constraints around model quantization and quality regression monitoring? We need guardrails to ensure output quality isn't degraded by quantization.
47:42 Mira: We'll include a quality baseline evaluation in the preflight and add regression alerts into Redwood Optimize; if quantization causes issues we can toggle back to FP16 paths.

50:05 Samir: Ok thanks everyone. Let's lock 3 deliverables: redlined MSA/DPA (Jordan), pricing (Jordan/Pricing), benchmark run (Mira).
50:17 Jordan: Agreed. Diego will help coordinate the onboarding tasks.
50:25 Diego: I'll follow up with a checklist and an initial timeline.

52:00 Jordan: Thanks all. We'll send notes and action items. If there's anything urgent ping me; otherwise look for the docs by end of day Saturday.
52:12 Lina: Thanks.
52:15 Olivia: Thanks all.
52:20 Daniel: Bye.
52:22 Samir: Bye.
